MARKET OVERVIEW

1. What is the Current Market Regime?
Supplied regime: NEUTRAL, with normal volatility at 29.1% and weak participation: 0/8 sectors positive over one week. The inputs do not fit the stated neutral rule of normal volatility plus mixed breadth, so the regime label merits review.

2. Which sectors are leading?
Transportation leads on a relative basis despite a negative week: PGSUS (1W: -2.58% | 1M: +21.19%) CORRECTION and THYAO (1W: -3.78% | 1M: +20.62%) CORRECTION. Construction & REIT follows; ALARK (1W: -3.03% | 1M: +0.66%) and TKFEN (1W: -3.47% | 1M: +2.80%) are both in CORRECTION.

3. Which sectors are lagging?
Technology & Telecom is weakest on a weekly sector basis, followed by Retail & Food and Heavy Industry. KONTR (1W: -16.73% | 1M: +64.75%) CORRECTION and MGROS (1W: -11.92% | 1M: -4.89%) BELOW TREND highlight the sharp drawdowns.

STOCK PERFORMANCE

4. Top Performing Stocks?
Best relative weekly performers: PGSUS (1W: -2.58% | 1M: +21.19%) CORRECTION, ALARK (1W: -3.03% | 1M: +0.66%) CORRECTION, GUBRF (1W: -3.35% | 1M: -2.64%) BELOW TREND, TKFEN (1W: -3.47% | 1M: +2.80%) CORRECTION and TAVHL (1W: -3.61% | 1M: +5.25%) CORRECTION. All five still fell over the week.

5. Worst Performing Stocks?
Largest weekly declines: KONTR (1W: -16.73% | 1M: +64.75%) CORRECTION, TRMET (1W: -13.28% | 1M: -5.17%) BELOW TREND, VESTL (1W: -12.53% | 1M: -1.80%) BELOW TREND, MGROS (1W: -11.92% | 1M: -4.89%) BELOW TREND and ULKER (1W: -10.22% | 1M: -18.38%) BELOW TREND.

6. Momentum Stocks?
Relative weekly resilience is concentrated in PGSUS (1W: -2.58% | 1M: +21.19%) CORRECTION, ALARK (1W: -3.03% | 1M: +0.66%) CORRECTION and TKFEN (1W: -3.47% | 1M: +2.80%) CORRECTION. No stock posted a positive 1W return in the supplied top-performer list.

SECTOR OUTLOOK

7. Banking Sector Outlook?
Banking averaged -6.87% over one week and -2.40% over one month. AKBNK (1W: -9.61% | 1M: -6.69%) BELOW TREND and ISCTR (1W: -6.49% | 1M: -3.59%) BELOW TREND remain weak, while GARAN (1W: -5.35% | 1M: +7.07%) is in CORRECTION.

8. Industrial Sector Outlook?
Heavy Industry fell 8.40% over one week, with all supplied key names below their monthly levels except TOASO. EREGL (1W: -8.08% | 1M: -7.06%) BELOW TREND and FROTO (1W: -7.85% | 1M: -1.55%) BELOW TREND contrast with TOASO (1W: -3.68% | 1M: +6.16%) CORRECTION.

9. Energy & Chemicals Outlook?
The sector lost 7.95% over one week and 10.14% over one month. TUPRS (1W: -8.03% | 1M: -12.76%) BELOW TREND and SISE (1W: -10.01% | 1M: -12.15%) BELOW TREND remain under pressure; GUBRF (1W: -3.35% | 1M: -2.64%) BELOW TREND was a relative outperformer.

PORTFOLIO STRATEGY

10. Portfolio Recommendation?
Keep risk exposure measured and prioritize liquidity while breadth remains 0/8 and all sector quant screens are disqualified. Avoid treating monthly gains as confirmation where the weekly trend has reversed; wait for breadth improvement before adding cyclical exposure.

NEXT WEEK OUTLOOK

11. Stocks to Watch Next Week?
Track whether monthly leaders stabilize: PGSUS (1W: -2.58% | 1M: +21.19%) CORRECTION and THYAO (1W: -3.78% | 1M: +20.62%) CORRECTION. Also watch TOASO (1W: -3.68% | 1M: +6.16%) CORRECTION for relative resilience and KONTR (1W: -16.73% | 1M: +64.75%) CORRECTION for elevated reversal risk.

12. Sectors to Watch Next Week?
Monitor Transportation for stabilization after the strongest relative weekly performance, and Banking for signs of selling pressure easing. Technology & Telecom warrants close attention given its weakest weekly sector return and wide dispersion between monthly and weekly performance.

13. Key Levels & Triggers?
No XU100 price levels or technical support/resistance data were supplied, so specific index levels cannot be stated. Key triggers are a turn to positive sector breadth and stabilization in weekly returns; persistent 0/8 breadth would reinforce the defensive stance.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

Normal volatility at 29.1% is paired with no positive sectors, leaving participation exceptionally weak; the supplied NEUTRAL label also conflicts with the stated regime rules. Transportation names and TOASO show relative resilience, but remain in CORRECTION, while broad sector weakness and sharp drawdowns argue for disciplined, selective risk-taking.
